summary: Spec fidelity (brief F2 'the commit takes the write lock first, recomputes the plan under it'; spec 12.7 MUST): in a repository that has no .canon/repo-write.lock (every repository set up by 0.34 until canon init is run again or a lock-taking write happens), the MUST is not met. Real binary on a copy of a repo with the file deleted: a refused commit (PLAN_STALE) and a preview create nothing, finding add and dispatch begin run with no lock and create no file (hold_existing_within returns None), and a destructive commit computes and gates its plan with no lock, then creates the file in Plan::hold and takes it only from the gate on. So for the first commit the plan is not recomputed under the lock and a writer that does not lock (all of them, there being no file) can change what the plan read between the recompute and the gate. The CHANGELOG states it ('re-run canon init once in a repository set up by 0.34'; init does make the file and the .gitignore line, checked) but the contract has no exception for that, and the fix is small: take the lock on a file that always exists (canon.yaml, or the .canon directory) or create the lock file for a destructive commit before the recompute and accept that a refused commit leaves one empty gitignored file. Blast radius: the first destructive commit after an upgrade; scenario 08 and the unit tests build their repos with the file in place.
